# Acquired local frames followed by standard five-qubit protection

28 October2026. New complete instance, independent review pending. The protocol is frozen in PREDECLARATION.json before its actual calibration and holdout draws. It is a software-simulated stationary source with ideal trusted controls, not a hardware or fault-tolerance demonstration.

Five physical qubit channels independently apply unknown-axis amplitude damping followed by unknown fixed rotations. The source rates are approximately.00995–.01550. Generator/scorer code knows them to implement the physical experiment; the learner receives only ordinary six-state input/random-Pauli output counts. It fits the3-by-3 Bloch response, takes its proper orthogonal polar factor, and synthesizes an exactly rational SU2 frame through stereographic coordinates. Its inverse is a physical unitary on every record. No source parameter, protected reference or exact noise model enters the learner.

Two independent fixed calibration budgets,4096 and16384 shots per site, produce two separate frozen pipelines. Each prepares the standard[[5,1,3]] code, sends five physical qubits through the five actual noisy channels, applies the five acquired inverses, and uses the known16-syndrome recovery. The code's stabilizers and logical conventions are copied from the separately reviewed governing worker source, with its exact program hash in PREDECLARATION.json. Exact Pauli-transfer polynomials are checked against the actual32-dimensional encoder/noise/recovery computation, including nonunital and non-Pauli terms. This is not a first-order or Pauli-twirled surrogate channel.

Fresh logical holdout trials prepare independent uniformly random members of the six Pauli eigenstates and measure the returned logical qubit in the matching basis. 28 October 2026. **Author result; independent full-pipeline audit pending.**

The frozen two-pipeline experiment completed without retries or discarded banks. Both actual learned receivers passed the predeclared logical entanglement-fidelity target **F_e >= 0.999**. The selected receiver used **4,096 calibration transmissions per physical site**, not an exact supplied frame. This is a small, complete acquisition-to-protection software instance, rather than a uniform inverse-error estimate.

| Calibration shots/site | Fresh logical failures / 131,072 | Fixed acceptance threshold | Post hoc exact logical infidelity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4,096 (selected) | 44 | <=52 | 0.0005180078319230905 |
| 16,384 | 48 | <=52 | 0.0004084269816334440 |

The exact-channel scores are diagnostics unavailable to the learner and are not the certificate. The certificate uses actual independent randomized six-state input/readout records after the receiver is frozen. The nominal failure probability is `(2/3)(1-F_e)`. Exact integer binomial tests, selection among both receivers, and all ten unencoded comparisons are protected by a twelve-test allocation of `3/5000`, plus sampling-record total variation `249/1099511627776` (about 2.27e-10). This is below the declared overall allowance 0.001. It is simultaneous frequentist coverage, not posterior certainty about these accepted records.

All five unencoded SAME-learned-inverse receivers in each bank separately confirmed **F_e <= 0.997**. Their failure counts were `[238,250,283,367,448]` and `[202,287,271,301,330]`, each out of 65,536; the predeclared threshold was >=179. This comparison does not upper-bound arbitrary unencoded CPTP recovery or compare equal transmission rates: one encoded qubit uses five physical channels and trusted encoding/recovery resources. The equally informed conventional procedure—ordinary Bloch-response fitting, polar frame calibration and the standard five-qubit code—is exactly this pipeline. No new code, optimizer advantage or conventional-method separation is claimed.

# Optional reduced-channel deployment corollary: private logical Pauli randomization

28 October 2026. **Separate derived interface, independent review pending.** This was not physically executed or added to the frozen pilot, and it is not needed for that pilot's fidelity certificate.

Let L be the actual fixed one-qubit logical CPTP channel after the acquired frames, encoder, physical noise and known decoder have been fixed. Suppose its independently validated entanglement fidelity obeys F_e(L)>=1-epsilon. For each subsequent use choose P uniformly from {I,X,Y,Z}, independently of inputs, source and all other trials. Apply P before encoding and P after decoding; actually retire the private key after both operations. Keeping it available to a future controller under the name of a Pauli frame is not retirement. The effective reduced logical channel is

    L_tw(rho) = (1/4) sum_P P L(P rho P) P.

This requires two fresh private random bits and two trusted physical implementations of logical Pauli controls per transmitted qubit (identity choices may be omitted physically), plus communicating the key to the receiver through the existing trusted controller or an explicitly paid private control interface. It is not free if transmitter and receiver are separated. The source must implement the same fixed channel regardless of the private key; a key-responsive source is outside the assumption.

## Derivation

Write a Kraus operator as K_a=sum_Q k_(a,Q) Q in the Pauli basis, orthonormal for the normalized Hilbert–Schmidt inner product Tr(A^dagger B)/2, with k_(a,Q)=Tr(Q K_a)/2. Pauli conjugation multiplies each coefficient by its character. The uniform character average cancels every unequal pair Q != Q', giving

    L_tw(rho)=sum_Q p_Q Q rho Q,
    p_Q=sum_a |k_(a,Q)|^2 >=0,   sum_Q p_Q=1.

Trace preservation gives the normalization. Its identity probability is p_I=sum_a |Tr K_a|^2/4=F_e(L), so entanglement fidelity is unchanged. For a Pauli channel,

    (1/2)||L_tw-id||_diamond = 1-p_I.

The upper bound follows from the triangle inequality: the identity component cancels, and each nonidentity Pauli unitary channel differs from identity by diamond norm at most2. For the matching lower bound, apply the channel to half of a Bell state. The four Pauli images are mutually orthogonal Bell states, so the output trace distance from the original Bell state is exactly1-p_I.
